title: Surge-aware prefetch scheduler and staged KV hydration to reduce cold starts
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets currently see long tail cold-starts during sudden tenant surge events. Cold starts are caused by (1) model weight residency misses on GPUs, (2) KV cache coldness for common prefixes, and (3) autoscaler ramp delay when burst capacity is requested. These manifests as request latency spikes that violate throughput SLAs and increase customer retries.

Goal: Deliver a production-safe scheduler that proactively stages model weights and hydrates KV shards ahead of anticipated demand spikes while minimizing wasted residency and cost. The feature must integrate with autoscaling signals, provide tenant-aware prioritization, and expose observability to SLOs and cost metrics.

Design summary: Implement a surge-aware prefetch scheduler (SAPS) with three coordinated mechanisms:
  1) Predictive ingress windowing: use short-term traffic forecasts (per-tenant top-k routes over the last 60s) to compute a ranked list of model variants and KV shards likely to be used. Forecast engine uses lightweight exponential smoothing + rate-of-change heuristics so it runs in the control plane with <50ms decision latency.
  2) Staged weight residency: instead of full eager loads, we stage model artifacts in layers: embedding + first N transformer blocks + KV-only layers. Scheduler uses a priority threshold so high-probability models get full residency, medium probability get partial staged residency to allow immediate minimal-latency inference while the remaining weights stream in.
  3) Bucketed KV hydration: KV cache is partitioned into hot/mid/cold buckets. Hydration happens in order of expected token prefix hit-rate: hot prefixes (top 1%) are hydrated first, mid (next 9%) next. Hydration is incremental and can be throttled by cost budget or node pressure.

Integration with autoscaler and fleet controls: SAPS signals the Dedicated autoscaler to pre-allocate burst-capacity nodes into a warm standby state (GPU reservations with deferred full weight residency). Admission controller enforces tenant-level throughput guarantees so low-tier tenants cannot trigger full residency by spike alone. Eviction policy correlates with observed steady-state TTL and cross-tenant sharing benefit score.

Observability and SLOs: track p50/p95/p99 cold-start latency, model residency hit-rate, KV prefix hit-rate, prefetch success ratio, and incremental cost (GPU-minutes). Add dashboards and alerts when prefetch cost exceeds configured budget or when prediction accuracy drops below threshold.

Rationale: Existing approaches either fully preheat broad warm pools (high cost) or rely purely on reactive loading (high latency). This hybrid, surge-aware approach seeks the Pareto point between cost and SLO by allocating partial residency and prioritizing hydration by expected hit-rate.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment of SAPS to staging cluster behind feature flag
End-to-end test showing cold-start p95 reduction by >= 3x for simulated tenant surge (internal replication harness)
Integration with dedicated autoscaler to pre-allocate warm-standby nodes on forecasted surge within 20s of signal
Dashboard with residency hit-rate, KV hydration progress, prefetch cost; automated alert on prefetch-cost > budget
Canary rollout plan documented and rollback path validated
Documentation for operators and runbook for eviction and budget tuning
comments: 2026-03-01: Initial spike analysis completed by Marcus. Median cold-start for production traces: 9.7s, p95: 27.2s. Identified top-3 routes responsible for 62% of surge traffic.
2026-03-04: Design review w/ PM and Runtime team. Decided to avoid ML-heavy forecasting in v1; use lightweight EWMA + delta heuristics. Action: prototype forecast module (Ayesha).
2026-03-07: Prototype of staged weight loader merged to internal branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892
2026-03-09: Simulated surge test in CI showed median cold-start improvement from 9.7s -> 2.8s when partial staging enabled; cost overhead measured at +7% GPU-minutes for the test workload.
2026-03-11: Ops requested per-tenant prefetch budget and hard cap. Added budget enforcement to scheduler config (per-tenant and fleet-level).

2026-03-14: Running extended soak in staging with variable tenant mixes. Observed degraded hydra accuracy when request patterns shift rapidly; mitigations: shorten forecast window and increase re-eval frequency to 15s. Next: tune eviction TTLs and run multi-tenant cost simulation.
changes: Implement forecast engine in control plane (Ayesha)
Add staged weight loader API to runtime (Marcus)
Partition KV cache into hot/mid/cold and implement ordered hydrator (engineer: Lucia)
Autoscaler hook to pre-allocate warm-standby nodes (engineer: Raj)
Admission controller update to enforce tenant throughput caps during prefetch
Operator UI: expose prefetch budget and visualization in Console
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind sap-scheduler FF for dedicated fleets
Canary: enable for 5 internal customers with predictable workloads for 72h
Gradual ramp to 25% of fleets with active monitoring for prefetch cost and latency
If prefetch cost > budget or prediction accuracy < 40% during canary, roll back SAPS and collect traces
Full rollout contingent on <10% cost overhead at fleet-level and p95 cold-start reduction >= 2.5x
